Due July 2, 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31, paid to the Province — a different second-stage date than Chilliwack's August 4 and a different structure than Mission's flat 10%, on properties whose mailing addresses name both of those cities' regions.

Freshet alerts have named these exact streets. FVRD freshet evacuation alerts for Area G have covered Nicomen Island and the Taylor Road area in Deroche, and Dewdney Regional Park has appeared among flood-related park closures — flood diligence here is historical fact, not a formality.

items.t: Every first-page card is labelled with the board sub-area "Dewdney Deroche" and a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Lougheed Highway, Taylor Road, Bergen Road, Cooper Road and Ridgeview Road.

What the page covers — IDENTITY CALL: the two rural communities of Dewdney and Deroche along the Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) corridor east of Mission. It does not cover land inside the City of Mission, despite the "Mission" mailing addresses and the page title's "Mission BC" wording.

Board geography: in the board data, "Dewdney Deroche" is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Mission" — a reporting grouping only; it does not make Dewdney or Deroche part of the City of Mission.

Ministry-listed names only are used. School-district coverage (SD75) and municipal governance are different things — SD75 serves these FVRD communities even though the City of Mission does not govern them, and Area G voters elect an SD75 rural trustee. Catchments: no SD75 catchment document or locator run for an address here is on record, so catchment schools for any specific address are not verified.

Servicing frame: FVRD bylaws provide for a Deroche water system and an Electoral Area G Dewdney Community Water System — servicing runs through FVRD systems where a lot is inside a service area, not through the City of Mission. Whether a specific lot is on a community system, a private well, or a community sewer vs septic: Not verified at parcel level.

items.t: Form B diligence — stated with its limit: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no application to the fee-simple acreages and pad-rent manufactured homes that make up this corridor's stock — there is no verified strata building here for it to attach to. If a listing in this corridor ever presents as strata, the Form B is the first document to demand, precisely because no strata stock is verified here.

Rental and age bylaws (strata law, for contrast): strata rental-restriction bylaws have been VOID since Nov 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, and only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful in a strata (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Fee-simple position — the corridor's actual default: A fee-simple purchase here carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees; FVRD zoning, registered covenants and provincial rural rules govern instead. The corridor's houses and acreages are that product.

Planning and zoning (local): FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern this Electoral Area G ground. Confirm a parcel's designation and zone with the FVRD for the PID. Mission's OCP 6405-2026 does NOT apply here — that is City of Mission ground, west of this corridor.

Rural property taxes — the regime that actually applies: a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or the City of Mission. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s. 11, rural property taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on October 31. Mission's flat 10% penalty is expressly DISAPPLIED here — it is a City of Mission rule for city ground, and Dewdney-Deroche is not city ground; Chilliwack's August second-stage date does not apply here either.

ALR housing rules: parcel-level ALR status is per PID: Not verified — check the parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission mapping. Where land is in the ALR: generally one principal residence capped at 500 m² total floor area, plus at most one additional residence up to 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha); and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).

items.t: Planning and zoning framework — FVRD, numbers not verified: No Chilliwack bylaw number and no Mission bylaw number is borrowed for this ground, and the one zoning label in the feed ("FVRD C-2," listing text) is not adopted. The process is what is documented: zoning, permits and servicing questions for a parcel go to the FVRD as the local government for Electoral Area G, confirmed per PID before any build, subdivision or second-dwelling plan is priced.

Subdivision / servicing — process documented, no bylaw number asserted: no FVRD subdivision-servicing bylaw number is verified for this ground (Not verified, above), so the documented position is procedural: subdivision of a Dewdney-Deroche parcel runs through the FVRD/provincial approving process for electoral-area ground, with servicing proven parcel by parcel — community water where the lot is inside an FVRD service area (Deroche water system; Electoral Area G Dewdney Community Water System), otherwise private well and septic, each not verified at parcel level until the specific lot's service-area position is confirmed with the FVRD.

Flood diligence — the corridor's defining land check: the FVRD has issued freshet evacuation alerts for Area G ground including Nicomen Island and the Taylor Road area in Deroche, and the lowland parts of this corridor are Fraser River floodplain ground.

ALR block (provincial frame, for the corridor's farmland parcels): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).
Second dwellings on non-ALR ground: Confirm with the FVRD per PID.

Rural property taxes — the jurisdiction rule in full: a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or the City of Mission. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, rural property taxes are due and payable on July 2 of the year they are first levied, a 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on October 31. The City of Mission's flat 10% penalty after July 2 does NOT apply here — tax follows the jurisdiction (FVRD Electoral Area G / rural provincial), not the Mission mailing address.

items.t: The mailing address is the trap. Every listing here carries a Mission address, the page title says "Mission BC," and the editorial heading calls this "Mission's Rural Frontier" — and none of it governs anything. The FVRD is the local government, the Province collects the tax, and Mission's bylaws, OCP and flat 10% tax penalty stop at the city boundary.
The tax penalty calendar is split, not flat.

The Deroche Bench crosses an electoral-area line. The eastern portions of the Deroche Bench sit in Electoral Area C, not Area G — two otherwise similar bench parcels can answer to different FVRD plan areas, and which side of the G/C line a specific parcel sits on is not verified at parcel level. Check the electoral area for the PID, not the community name.

"Area G" is not a unique bylaw address. At least two other BC regional districts (Nanaimo; Okanagan-Similkameen) also have an Electoral Area G with its own OCP bylaws — a web search for "Area G OCP bylaw" returns those districts' numbers, which have nothing to do with Dewdney or Deroche.
One park, two products. An age label for this corridor is read off the park's own rules, in writing.

Water is a service-area question, not a community question. Both Dewdney and Deroche have FVRD community water systems on the FVRD's own bylaw record — and lots outside the service areas are on wells. "Deroche has community water" is true and useless; the parcel's service-area position is the fact that matters.

Floodplain is the corridor's standing condition (2022 freshet record, read Nov 1, 2026). FVRD freshet alerts have covered Nicomen Island and the Taylor Road area in Deroche, and Dewdney Regional Park is listed among flood-related park closures — lowland pricing that ignores dyke and flood-construction diligence is mispricing.

Guide-only claims (the Area G census figures, Dewdney Regional Park address/hours, Inch Creek Hatchery details, Dewdney Area Improvement District figures, the Area G OCP Bylaw No. 0866 citation, the Hatzic Middle catchment assertion, and the Mission Senior Secondary replacement funding figures) are not verified site copy, not defects and not facts.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Dewdney-Deroche

What acreage actually trades in Dewdney-Deroche: fee-simple rural acreage — whole parcels and acreage-with-house listings along the Lougheed corridor. Acreage IS the fee-simple market here, in process terms.
The ground in Dewdney-Deroche

items.t: Fee-simple acreages — the substance: No area-wide lot-size profile is published by any official source — lot sizes and age/style profile are not verified as area figures, and BC Assessment data is property-by-property. No typical size is invented.
Manufactured-home parks: A home on a rented pad is not lot stock / land / acreage.

Serviced vs unserviced: FVRD community water systems exist for Deroche and for Dewdney in Area G, but not every lot is inside a service area — confirm water source, sewer vs septic, and any system fees for the specific parcel with the FVRD before writing. Parcel-level position: Not verified.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Dewdney-Deroche

items.t: JURISDICTION LOCK, restated: Dewdney and Deroche are unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area G communities along the Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) corridor east of Mission. The FVRD's Electoral Areas Housing Needs Report lists “Electoral Area G: Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island.” The FVRD, not the City of Mission, is the local government; City of Mission bylaws, zoning and tax rules do not apply here.
The page does not cover land inside the City of Mission, despite the “Mission” mailing addresses and the page title's “Mission BC” wording.

Eastern edge: the FVRD Electoral Area C plan area begins east of Deroche — it “spans from the Harrison River to the east of Deroche and includes Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock, and the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench,” so the easternmost Deroche Bench ground sits in Area C, not Area G. Which side of the G/C line a specific parcel sits on: Not verified at parcel level.
Mission community figures are board context for a city market to the west, not Dewdney-Deroche figures, and are not presented as this market's figures here.

Schools are SD75 Mission — district coverage and municipal governance are different things. Ministry-listed names only: Dewdney Elementary, 37151 Hawkins-Pickle Rd, Dewdney; Deroche Elementary, 10340 N Deroche Rd, Deroche; Hatzic Middle School, 34875 Moffat Avenue, Mission; Mission Senior Secondary, 32939 7th Ave, Mission. The FVRD's election notice places Deroche (Area G) voters in the SD75 rural trustee election.

Community water frame: FVRD bylaws provide for a Deroche water system and an Electoral Area G Dewdney Community Water System — servicing runs through FVRD systems where a lot is inside a service area, not through the City of Mission. Parcel-level position: Not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Dewdney-Deroche

items.t: The Deroche Bench crosses an electoral-area line: Eastern portions of the Deroche Bench are in Area C, not Area G — two parcels that read as one bench can sit under two different FVRD plan areas, and the side for a specific parcel is not verified until checked.

Water is a service-area question, not a community question: Both communities have FVRD community water systems on the FVRD's bylaw record — and lots outside the service areas are on wells. “Deroche has community water” is true and useless; the parcel's service-area position is the fact that matters.
One park, two products in listing text: An age label is read off the park's own rules, in writing.
